pubcol-w-fc73c187c1b5dcec.definition_en: to make changes to something, often to clothes or a design
pubcol-w-fc73c187c1b5dcec.example_simple: The tailor will make alterations to the jacket so it fits me better.
pubcol-w-fc73c187c1b5dcec.example_complex: Before the building could be reopened, the architect had to make substantial alterations to the original plans to meet safety regulations.

pubcol-w-454998f5ea8d408d.definition_en: to do something to make up for a wrong or harm you have caused
pubcol-w-454998f5ea8d408d.example_simple: He sent flowers to make amends for forgetting her birthday.
pubcol-w-454998f5ea8d408d.example_complex: Determined to make amends for the harm his company had caused, the director set up a fund to support the affected families.

pubcol-w-fc9e145c43cbf3da.definition_en: to compensate someone for a wrong or loss you have caused them
collocations: make amends to him for the trouble
make amends to someone for the loss
want to make amends to sb for
pubcol-w-fc9e145c43cbf3da.example_simple: She wanted to make amends to her neighbour for breaking his window.
pubcol-w-fc9e145c43cbf3da.example_complex: The airline promised to make amends to the stranded passengers for the delay by offering full refunds and hotel accommodation.

pubcol-w-d90f2a2679bf74c6.definition_en: to tell people about something officially or publicly
pubcol-w-d90f2a2679bf74c6.example_simple: The teacher stood up to make an announcement about the school trip.
pubcol-w-d90f2a2679bf74c6.example_complex: The government is expected to make a major announcement regarding the new tax policy later this week.

pubcol-w-000bf99ac2e6bbc6.definition_en: to arrange a fixed time to meet or see someone
collocations: make an appointment with the doctor
pubcol-w-000bf99ac2e6bbc6.example_simple: I need to make an appointment with the dentist next week.
pubcol-w-000bf99ac2e6bbc6.example_complex: If you wish to discuss your results in detail, please make an appointment with your tutor during office hours.

pubcol-w-befe8382bba85c68.definition_en: to begin something, especially a journey, early in the day
collocations: make an early start on the journey
make an early start in the morning
want to make an early start
pubcol-w-befe8382bba85c68.example_simple: We should make an early start so we can avoid the traffic.
pubcol-w-befe8382bba85c68.example_complex: Knowing how long the hike would take, the group decided to make an early start and set off before dawn.

pubcol-w-cf8c4d7667389d51.definition_en: to try hard to do something
pubcol-w-cf8c4d7667389d51.example_simple: You should make an effort to speak English every day.
pubcol-w-cf8c4d7667389d51.example_complex: Despite her busy schedule, she always makes an effort to attend every meeting and support her colleagues.

pubcol-w-2a831d0d78f3e605.definition_en: to make something better than it was before
pubcol-w-2a831d0d78f3e605.example_simple: The new teacher helped him make an improvement in his grades.
pubcol-w-2a831d0d78f3e605.example_complex: By investing in modern equipment, the factory managed to make a dramatic improvement in both productivity and safety.

pubcol-w-690a7a16eb9352cd.definition_en: to write a plan showing the main points of something
collocations: make an outline of the essay
pubcol-w-690a7a16eb9352cd.example_simple: Before writing the essay, I like to make an outline of my ideas.
pubcol-w-690a7a16eb9352cd.example_complex: The researcher was advised to make a clear outline of her argument before drafting the full thesis chapter.

pubcol-w-7cd935399edde2f1.definition_en: to organise or plan the details needed for something to happen
pubcol-w-7cd935399edde2f1.example_simple: We need to make arrangements for the party this weekend.
pubcol-w-7cd935399edde2f1.example_complex: The embassy will make arrangements for the safe return of the citizens stranded abroad.

pubcol-w-e4d981c67e2e93d5.definition_en: to behave as though something were true; to pretend to do something
collocations: make as if nothing had happened
pubcol-w-e4d981c67e2e93d5.example_simple: He made as if to leave, then sat back down.
pubcol-w-e4d981c67e2e93d5.example_complex: She made as if she hadn't heard the insult, calmly continuing her presentation as though nothing had happened.

pubcol-w-5232c40cb5a27b7c.definition_en: to pretend that something imaginary is real, especially in play
pubcol-w-5232c40cb5a27b7c.example_simple: The children like to make believe they are pirates on a ship.
pubcol-w-5232c40cb5a27b7c.example_complex: For a few hours they could make believe the war had never happened and that their old life was waiting to be resumed.

pubcol-w-1eca552468dfb9da.definition_en: to earn just enough money to cover one's basic expenses
collocations: struggle to make both ends meet
work hard to make both ends meet
pubcol-w-1eca552468dfb9da.example_simple: After losing his job, it was hard to make both ends meet.
pubcol-w-1eca552468dfb9da.example_complex: With prices rising faster than wages, many families are finding it increasingly difficult to make both ends meet each month.

pubcol-w-2f5fa98d2fc3ee1e.example_simple: My grandmother taught me how to make bread from scratch.
pubcol-w-2f5fa98d2fc3ee1e.example_complex: During the lockdown, many people took up baking and learned to make bread using traditional sourdough methods.

pubcol-w-3748258141e36161.definition_en: to work out an amount or result using numbers
collocations: make a calculation of the cost
pubcol-w-3748258141e36161.example_simple: The engineer had to make a calculation of the total weight.
pubcol-w-3748258141e36161.example_complex: Before approving the budget, the accountant made a careful calculation of the projected costs for the entire year.

pubcol-w-899212ed99b75fab.definition_en: to unite with someone to achieve a shared aim
collocations: make common cause with the opposition
pubcol-w-899212ed99b75fab.example_simple: The two parties made common cause with each other to defeat the plan.
pubcol-w-899212ed99b75fab.example_complex: Former enemies made common cause with one another, setting aside old grievances to confront the greater threat they now shared.

pubcol-w-558e592ea19c0a8a.definition_en: to unite with others in pursuit of a common goal
collocations: make common cause against a rival
make common cause on the issue
pubcol-w-558e592ea19c0a8a.example_simple: The workers made common cause with the students during the protest.
pubcol-w-558e592ea19c0a8a.example_complex: Environmental groups made common cause with local farmers, recognising that both stood to lose if the river was polluted.

pubcol-w-a00646d552476925.definition_en: to examine how something is similar to or different from someone or something else
collocations: make a comparison with the original
pubcol-w-a00646d552476925.example_simple: It is useful to make a comparison with last year's results.
pubcol-w-a00646d552476925.example_complex: In her essay, she makes an insightful comparison with the works of earlier poets to highlight the writer's originality.

pubcol-w-b13d9082004686e5.definition_en: to give money, help, or ideas towards something
pubcol-w-b13d9082004686e5.example_simple: Everyone was asked to make a contribution to the charity.
pubcol-w-b13d9082004686e5.example_complex: Through her groundbreaking research, she made a lasting contribution to our understanding of the human brain.

pubcol-w-23ec5149e4f4643f.definition_en: to earn just enough money to pay for what one needs
collocations: work hard to make ends meet
pubcol-w-23ec5149e4f4643f.example_simple: They both work two jobs just to make ends meet.
pubcol-w-23ec5149e4f4643f.example_complex: As the cost of living soared, even well-qualified professionals found it a struggle to make ends meet.

pubcol-w-ddcc317cff331512.definition_en: to help to produce or bring about a particular result
pubcol-w-ddcc317cff331512.example_simple: Good communication makes for a happy team.
pubcol-w-ddcc317cff331512.example_complex: The combination of clever writing and strong performances makes for one of the most compelling dramas of the year.

pubcol-w-17b43f27701d33ba.definition_en: to use or treat something freely, often without permission or respect
collocations: make free with other people's things
pubcol-w-17b43f27701d33ba.example_simple: He tends to make free with other people's belongings.
pubcol-w-17b43f27701d33ba.example_complex: The guests made free with the host's fine wine, opening bottle after bottle as if it were their own.

pubcol-w-25e1e3046689c741.definition_en: to begin a friendship with someone
pubcol-w-25e1e3046689c741.example_simple: She quickly made friends with the new student in her class.
pubcol-w-25e1e3046689c741.example_complex: Living abroad taught him how to make friends with people from very different cultural backgrounds.

pubcol-w-9a639c91546c19ca.definition_en: to laugh at someone or something in an unkind way
collocations: make fun of the way he talks
pubcol-w-9a639c91546c19ca.example_simple: It's cruel to make fun of people because of how they look.
pubcol-w-9a639c91546c19ca.example_complex: The comedian built his entire routine around making fun of the absurd rituals of everyday office life.

pubcol-w-f49dde2e7e7380ff.definition_en: to succeed or become successful, especially after a difficult start
pubcol-w-f49dde2e7e7380ff.example_simple: He left his village poor but returned having made good in the city.
pubcol-w-f49dde2e7e7380ff.example_complex: The film tells the story of an immigrant who, against all odds, makes good and builds a thriving business from nothing.
